scope: Broaden open-source DWG/DXF peer research to FreeCAD's actual converter/importer route, importer-specific 3D scope, and peer writer loss; update existing parity and 3D plans without creating an external runtime dependency or promoting support.

method.kind: Primary application-source research, documentation cross-check, and local plan/source inspection
localInspection: DWG_DXF_OPEN_SOURCE_PARITY_PLAN.md: existing PAR-07/S8 carrier, identity, owner/block, and consumer gates
DWG_DXF_3D_SUPPORT_PLAN.md: existing FreeCAD and ACIS acceptance boundary
dwg2dxf/dx_iface.cpp and src/libdxfrw.cpp: local modeler carrier admission and DXF output handling
tests/dxf_fixture_tests.cpp and docs/research/deeper-broader-spline-leader-insert-table-peer-review-2026-10-17.json: current LEADER annotation test scope
method.sourceLimitations: FreeCAD application source is mutable main; Draft entity matrix and general format table were found in a GitHub-hosted documentation mirror and conflict with broader format wording. Neither source set was pinned to the target native FreeCAD build. ACadSharp issue #1195 is a reporter account without public customer drawings; PR #1240 is open and is not a released implementation.

evidence.topic: FreeCAD DWG import is converter plus selected DXF importer
evidence.observed: The current Draft importDWG.py locates and invokes external DWG converters; FreeCAD documentation lists LibreDWG, ODA File Converter, and QCAD Pro. FreeCAD's DXF documentation distinguishes the C++ importer from a more feature-complete legacy Python importer requiring a separate module.
doesNotEstablish: behavior of a particular installed OS/FreeCAD/converter/importer tuple
that converter success means DXF import or geometry import succeeded
DWG semantic support independent of the intervening DXF format/version
evidence.planUse: Bind native receipts to exact OS/build, converter/version/options, emitted DXF AC code, importer/backend/preferences, file hashes, diagnostics, and per-entity outcomes; keep direct DXF and converted DWG routes distinct.

evidence.topic: FreeCAD published DXF 3D-face scope is inconsistent and ACIS is a separate boundary
evidence.observed: A current general import/export documentation page describes DXF and DWG as 2D-only. A GitHub-hosted Draft DXF documentation mirror's importer table lists 3DFACE only for the legacy importer, and its text says binary ACIS/SAT solid carriers cannot currently be read by FreeCAD.
doesNotEstablish: current 3DFACE capability for an exact FreeCAD release/build
ACIS semantics in any separately installed modeler/plugin route
that a file opening or displaying wireframe proves entity-level fidelity
evidence.planUse: Record the 3DFACE scope as DOC_CONFLICT pending source inspection and a generated asymmetric native test. Keep stock ACIS consumer status not-applicable unless a named plugin is separately qualified.

evidence.topic: Peer entity recognition and writer omission do not prove 3D semantics
evidence.observed: ezdxf documents classes for modeler DXF entities, while its maintainer describes ACIS support as basic and warns that generated bodies may not behave as true volume-bearing solids. ACadSharp #1195 reports silent 3DSOLID/REGION omission, including solid-only blocks; its source drawings are unavailable and linked PR #1240 is not released. LibreDWG documents unknown classes preserved as opaque blobs without DXF codes and its release notes include route-specific SAT chunk-loss fixes.
doesNotEstablish: independent B-rep validity or CAD operation support from raw bytes/entity classes
equivalent behavior across peer versions or all DXF targets
evidence.planUse: Keep per-source handle and owner/block path disposition through carrier output, diagnostics, and independent reopen. Require fail-closed publication or explicit loss disposition; do not score opaque preservation as typed geometry semantics.

readinessRefinement: qualify FreeCAD by converter/importer route rather than application name alone
keep 3DFACE documentation conflict open until exact source/build test
separate explicit mesh and ACIS-carrier checks from B-rep semantics
retain generated block-only modeler loss controls and per-handle output accounting
perform native checks only at the composed checkpoint, not per code slice
